newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STATE COMMERCIAL BANK SALE TENDER EXTENDED.
newsitem.headline: STATE COMMERCIAL BANK SALE TENDER EXTENDED.

text.p: The government is to extend the deadline of the tender for the privatisation of the State Commercial Bank by one month.
The government announced a tender for 100 percent of the bank last month and the deadline to submit the bids expired at the start of July. However, no offers were received.

"We intend to extend the tender for around a month," Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta told a news conference late on Tuesday. Shemeta said the decision to extend the term for the tender will be taken this week.
He said the finance ministry will negotiate more intensively with potential investors both from Lithuania and abroad during the coming months.
Four potential investors bought the tender documents and Lithuania's Vilniaus Bankas and Hermis Bankas have said they were considering the idea of putting in a bid.
"It is not a secret that the price for the bank can be too high," Shemeta said when asked if the price asked would be a purely symbolic one.
The bank had nearly 173 million litas of losses in 1996 and a 6.1 million litas net profit in the first half of this year. It is one of two state banks that have been slated for sale.
